historical_claims.anchor: Davis and Kahan prove that distance-only separation always gives constant one in the Hilbert–Schmidt norm, and an operator-norm bound with an extra factor of the square root of the rank.
The two spectral-selection theorems of Section 8 use, respectively, an ordered gap between the reference blocks, and the doubled-sine hypothesis on the perturbed blocks
With only distance separation, neither argument applies, and the constant one fails in the operator norm. Davis and Kahan give a two by two example.
Davis and Kahan asked whether the square root of the rank could be replaced by a universal constant.
historical_claims.source_locator: Section 5 after (5.2); the pi/2 constant: Bhatia, Matrix Analysis, Section VII.2

related_resources.reason: General idea of a spectral gap; the lecture distinguishes three geometric shapes of separation that this article does not.
The Sylvester equation behind every gap estimate; the window argument is a Neumann-series style bound on its solution.
How eigenvalue gaps enter first-order eigenvector perturbation formulas, a heuristic for why separation controls subspace motion.
